sources.ref: Kiwi Ears web EQ (https://equalizer.kiwiears.com): the KT0211L register map, how it reads and writes the device, and its band editor

meta.notes: What Kiwi Ears' web app does: 5 peaking bands (its type selector is disabled and every Q write carries type 0), 20 to 20000 Hz in whole Hz, gain ±12 dB and Q 0.1 to 10, both to one decimal, with band frequencies kept strictly ascending (it sorts and rewrites a device that reads otherwise). It has no pre-gain and never touches register 0x66. Applying a preset turns the EQ on, writes each band 50 ms apart, each write waiting for its answer, saves to flash, then closes the device and reopens it 3 s later. Its Clear Flash button (command 0x43) isn't driven by the bridge. These are the app's editor limits, not verified firmware limits. devicePEQ differs: it offers low and high shelves as well (a shelf it wrote reads back on the Allegro Mini, whether it filters as one is unconfirmed), ±10 dB and Q to 5, treats register 0x24 as a preset slot (3 custom, 2 off) and sends writes without waiting for an answer. On the KT0211L, register 0x24 switches the EQ (1 on, 0 off; the Allegro Mini's other value, 3, sounds like neither, so nothing here writes it) and good writes answer with flag 3. Global Gain is register 0x3b (DacAnaGain_ALL) in 16 steps; the app writes it without saving, so it persists only with the next save.
